title: The Ambassador Ledger
notes: Source of truth for the public tracker. Featured AI/extra programs have fuller notes verified against official pages. Shorter cards cover the remainder of the geshan/developer-ambassador-programs list. Status is as of 31 Aug 2026. Do not invent deadlines or perks.

programs.name: ImagineArt Ambassador
programs.product: AI creative suite for images, video, voice, and film, ad, and fashion studios.
programs.whatTheyDo: Host meetups, workshops, and hackathons on campus or in a city; create with ImagineArt; run workshops that prototype AI art and design workflows; sit in feedback sessions that shape the product; swap notes with ambassadors in other cities through a private Discord.
programs.eligibility: Free, worldwide. Three tracks: community builders (meetups, campus or city groups, or a visible Discord/Reddit/X presence), top creators (consistent ImagineArt work plus community engagement), and students/campus leaders (enrolled at a university and growing AI art culture on campus). No professional title required. Other ambassadorships are allowed.
programs.perks: Event and challenge funding, ImagineArt Creator subscription, early models and beta features, official badge and featured profile, private Discord. High-performing ambassadors may be offered a full-time path. Official copy sometimes labels the badge as a Student Ambassador badge even though the program is not student-only.
programs.statusNote: No published deadline. Applications open as of 31 Aug 2026.

programs.name: Cloudflare Ambassadors 2026–27
programs.product: Developer platform and global network for sites, apps, Workers, and security at the edge.
programs.whatTheyDo: Bring Cloudflare into a campus, local organization, or city: host meetups, workshops, hackathons, or talks; publish tutorials or other content; be a visible helper in Cloudflare community spaces including Discord. Separate Community Engineers track (open-source grants) is not this cohort and opens later.
programs.eligibility: Student leaders, community organizers, and technical creators. Non-technical applicants are welcome. One-year cohort; can reapply for a second year. Not a paid role.
programs.perks: Meetup and workshop support; credits, marketing assets, and technical resources; access to Cloudflare expertise at events; recognition and exclusive swag. Ambassadors are not paid.
programs.statusNote: 2026–27 cohort. Apply by 6 Sep 2026. Selected ambassadors notified by 5 Oct 2026.

programs.name: Claude Community Ambassadors
programs.product: Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, including Claude Code and Claude Cowork.
programs.whatTheyDo: City hosts: run meetups, workshops, and hackathons; teach from live demos; bring community feedback to Anthropic product teams and Builders Council sessions; stay active in a private Slack with other ambassadors. This is not the closed student Campus program.
programs.eligibility: Meaningful experience with Claude Code or Claude Cowork plus a community track record. No developer title required. Global; multiple ambassadors per city welcome. Not paid. Other ambassadorships allowed except for companies whose core business competes with Anthropic.
programs.perks: Event funding, ready-to-use content, swag, promotion on Anthropic channels, monthly API credits, pre-release access, private Slack. No direct payment.
programs.statusNote: Applications open on a rolling basis. Membership continues while you host events and stay engaged.

programs.name: ElevenLabs Ambassador
programs.product: AI voice and audio platform for speech, agents, and media production.
programs.whatTheyDo: Community Builder track: host meetups, hackathons, demo nights, listening parties, and workshops. Content Creator track: publish tutorials, demos, workflow breakdowns, and reviews. You can apply to one track or both.
programs.eligibility: 18 or older with an active ElevenLabs account, something you have already made on the platform, and a real plan to contribute. Community program, not a paid role (content creators may unlock paid opportunities later). Affiliates program is separate and allowed.
programs.perks: Platform credits, early feature access, event funding, merch, support, invitations to ElevenLabs events. Exact mix depends on track and activity.
programs.statusNote: Applications open; team follows up with a short intro call if there is a fit.

programs.name: Factory Guild
programs.product: Factory / Droid — AI coding agents for software work.
programs.whatTheyDo: Public builders: ship writing, social posts, talks or workshops, or open-source work that shows Droid doing real work. New candidates interview with the Guild Council; returning members earn points and climb Apprentice → Craftsman → Artisan.
programs.eligibility: Council-vetted. Submissions must be public, specific, and reproducible. Not every submission is accepted.
programs.perks: Ranked credits (Max plan as Apprentice, Ultra as Craftsman, unlimited as Artisan), mentorship, swag kits, private Slack, early access. Higher ranks add 1:1s, events, travel stipend, and hiring fast-track as published on the Guild page.
programs.statusNote: Application form is live. Quality-gated, not automatic admission.

programs.name: Raycast Ambassadors
programs.product: macOS (and expanding) launcher with extensions and built-in AI.
programs.whatTheyDo: Host meetups, hackathons, and workshops; keep Slack and Reddit communities useful; teach others how to use Raycast; send product feedback.
programs.eligibility: Spaces are limited. Official FAQ covers acceptance criteria, notification timing, and commitment length on the program page.
programs.perks: Early access, free Raycast Pro including Advanced AI, event funding, merch, ambassador badge, private channel with the Raycast team.
programs.statusNote: Open with limited seats as of 31 Aug 2026. No public deadline posted.

programs.name: Pinecone Pioneers
programs.product: Managed vector database for retrieval, RAG, and knowledgeable AI.
programs.whatTheyDo: Builders, educators, and collaborators who share what they learned at least quarterly through posts, demos, or talks; support other builders; give product feedback.
programs.eligibility: Quality of work matters more than audience size. If you cannot share something at least quarterly, the page says it is probably not the right fit. You can apply once you have something to share.
programs.perks: Early access to select features, custom swag (annual), plaque for standout contributors, private channel, optional site profile, thought-leadership support including up to $500 travel to approved events.
programs.statusNote: Join the waitlist / apply for early access from the Pioneers page.

programs.name: Replit Community Ambassadors
programs.product: Cloud IDE and agent platform for building and shipping software in the browser.
programs.whatTheyDo: Host meetups, workshops, and hackathons; help other builders; share what you learn; welcome new people on Replit.
programs.eligibility: Builders who already use Replit and help others. The hub asks for people who publish content, foster communities, or host events. Reviews are monthly. Program copy has also said new ambassadors are admitted by invitational outreach, with a wider application window described as starting in early 2026 — treat it as rolling and invite-leaning.
programs.perks: Welcome pack if selected. Public hub mentions credits, swag, and early access as typical ambassador support; confirm current pack on apply.
programs.statusNote: Application form is live and reviewed on a rolling / monthly basis; admission is invite-leaning.

programs.name: Replit Creators
programs.product: Cloud IDE and agent platform; this track is a gated creator partnership, not the community ambassador program.
programs.whatTheyDo: Partner with Replit to teach, inspire, and show how to build and ship in public — tutorials, builds, and creator collaborations.
programs.eligibility: Audience gate: 10k+ YouTube subscribers or 20k+ followers on Instagram, LinkedIn, or TikTok, plus 5k+ average views across your last five videos or posts.
programs.perks: Official page describes collaboration with creators who teach and ship. Specific creator compensation is not listed as a public perk list on the eligibility block.
programs.statusNote: Apply on replit.com/creators if you meet the published thresholds.

programs.name: W&B Author Program
programs.product: ML experiment tracking, evaluation, and MLOps platform.
programs.whatTheyDo: Write supported technical pieces — guides, tutorials, or ML/MLOps essays — with W&B MLEs, SEO, and editors. Paid or otherwise supported writing, not a meetup-host ambassador title.
programs.eligibility: Writers with a sample and a topic they want to cover. Capacity-limited: only a few members at a time so the team can actually edit and support the work.
programs.perks: Editorial and SEO support, Slack access to W&B MLEs, distribution, swag, and pay for writing as described on the official page.
programs.statusNote: Form is live. If you do not hear back, they likely have no availability and will reach out when they do.

programs.name: AAIF Agentic AI Ambassador
programs.product: Linux Foundation home for agentic AI projects including MCP, Goose, and AGENTS.md.
programs.whatTheyDo: Project-based advocacy: one public contribution per month tied to an AAIF project — tutorial, meetup or conference talk, short video, blog post, livestream, or course — so other developers can understand, try, or contribute.
programs.eligibility: Practitioners with some mix of technical credibility, community presence, and educational content. You do not need every box. Initial published cohort size was 10.
programs.perks: Public recognition, private Discord, maintainer briefings, swag, discounted/VIP conference treatment, contribution badges, amplification through AAIF channels.
programs.statusNote: Applications accepted any time; reviewed at intake windows. Next published intake: January 2027.

programs.name: DeepLearning.AI Event Ambassador (Pie & AI)
programs.product: AI education company (courses and community) founded around Andrew Ng’s teaching.
programs.whatTheyDo: Host local Pie & AI / AI-ML meetups at least once a quarter, in person or virtual. You organize independently. DeepLearning.AI promotes the event; you fund it.
programs.eligibility: Passion for AI/ML; working in AI or transitioning into it; prior experience organizing at least one developer-centric event. Volunteer role — you are financially responsible for the event.
programs.perks: Promotion on DeepLearning.AI channels, course discounts for ambassadors and attendees, speaker connections, a greeting video from Andrew and the team, email support. Not event cash.
programs.statusNote: HubSpot apply form is live. No published deadline.

programs.name: Devin.ai Ambassador
programs.product: Devin, Cognition’s AI software engineer.
programs.whatTheyDo: Lead the Devin community in your city: host events, create content, and help shape what comes next.
programs.eligibility: City community leads. Official page copy is a short CTA rather than a long rubric — confirm current bar on the community page.
programs.perks: Not itemized on the short public CTA. Do not assume credits or pay unless the live page lists them.
programs.statusNote: Public apply CTA on the community page as of 31 Aug 2026. No deadline published.

programs.name: Kiro Ambassadors
programs.product: Kiro, an AI IDE / agentic coding environment from Amazon.
programs.whatTheyDo: Super-users and community builders: send regular quarterly feedback, join private betas, attend product/engineering calls, create Kiro content or host a community event at least monthly, share announcements, stay active on Discord.
programs.eligibility: Developers who already use Kiro as a real part of their workflow and already show up in communities (content, OSS, events, Discord/Reddit). Accepted ambassadors sign an NDA. One-year term; renewal based on contribution quality.
programs.perks: A full year of premium Kiro, early access / private betas, monthly product calls, event-support credits, Discord badge, private channel, content collaboration. Time estimate on the launch post: about 3–4 hours of ambassador-specific work per month plus ongoing usage.
programs.statusNote: Applications reviewed on a rolling basis. Apply at kiro.dev/ambassadors/apply/.

programs.name: Mistral AI Ambassadors
programs.product: Mistral models and le Chat — open-weight and hosted AI from Mistral.
programs.whatTheyDo: Answer community questions, write tutorials or other educational content, give product feedback, and show up at Mistral events as a representative.
programs.eligibility: Current official docs: genuine use of Mistral, AI/ML experience, prior public advocacy, and a willingness to commit at least six months. Applications reviewed continuously. Rolling intake.
programs.perks: Free API credits on Studio, early access and product-team discussions, public recognition, Discord/Slack channel, early event invites.
programs.statusNote: Docs state applications are open on a rolling basis as of 31 Aug 2026.

programs.name: n8n Ambassador
programs.product: Open-source workflow automation, including AI-agent workflows.
programs.whatTheyDo: Be the local face of n8n: host meetups, workshops, and other community events; connect builders; work with the n8n community team. n8n has said it funds events and provides playbooks, Slack, and swag.
programs.eligibility: Experienced n8n community members who already share knowledge and can run events. Public help-center copy does not list a numeric tenure or event quota; confirm any 12-month or events-per-year bar on the live apply form.
programs.perks: Community posts and DevRel write-ups mention event budget, swag, private Slack, Cloud/Enterprise licenses for educational use, and a site listing. Confirm the current pack on n8n.io/ambassadors.
programs.statusNote: Apply form on n8n.io/ambassadors. Help center: no published deadline; team follows up after you submit.

programs.name: Cursor Ambassador
programs.product: AI code editor.
programs.whatTheyDo: Help new users, host meetups/hackathons/workshops, share workflows, give product feedback, and keep community spaces useful. Separate Campus Leads program is student-only and runs fall/spring.
programs.eligibility: Main ambassador track: 18+, application form, code of conduct, willingness to moderate and host. Cursor prefers you not hold other advocacy programs at the same time. Campus Leads: students; applications reopen in January.
programs.perks: Nightly / early access, credits, forum badge and moderation, meetup funding and stickers, Slack with the team, merch.
programs.statusNote: Typeform / apply path closed as of 30 Aug 2026. Campus Leads reopen January (student-only).

programs.name: Codex Ambassadors
programs.product: OpenAI Codex, a coding agent for software development.
programs.whatTheyDo: Run hands-on Codex meetups and workshops; create reusable learning assets; grow local builder communities; send candid feedback to the Codex team. Published time ask: about 2–4 hours per week and one contribution per month.
programs.eligibility: Future cohorts: community organizers, open-source maintainers, student leaders, workshop facilitators, and Codex power users. Existing event-hosting experience helps but is not required.
programs.perks: Codex and API credits, starter kits, private line to ambassadors and the Codex team, exclusive events, swag, and an honorarium as listed on the official page.
programs.statusNote: Official page: applications are paused. Expressions of interest are not active applications while paused.

programs.name: Claude Campus
programs.product: Claude, aimed at student clubs and campus ambassadors — not the city Community Ambassador program.
programs.whatTheyDo: Lead a Claude Builder Club or act as a Campus Ambassador: set up a campus AI-builder org, run technical and non-technical workshops, hackathons, and demo nights, and share credits and resources with members.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Builder Club track mentions a paid stipend on the official page.
programs.perks: Anthropic support, collaboration with research/product/education teams, API credits for members. Builder Club lists a paid program stipend.
programs.statusNote: Spring 2026 program is in session. Official page: applications have closed.

programs.name: PyTorch Ambassador
programs.product: PyTorch (and sibling Foundation projects such as vLLM) — open-source ML framework and ecosystem.
programs.whatTheyDo: Local community leadership (at least one event per quarter), stay current via Foundation sessions, write tutorials or talks, mentor new users, and contribute to the open-source ecosystem. Two-year term. About 5–10 hours per month.
programs.eligibility: 18+, Code of Conduct and LF antitrust, demonstrated PyTorch technical work (OSS, teaching, or user-group leadership).
programs.perks: Title and site feature, private Slack, playbooks, approved expense reimbursement, free PyTorch Conference entrance, swag.
programs.statusNote: 2026 applications closed 18 Jun 2026, 11:59 PM PDT. Notifications listed as September 2026; 2026 cohort announced October 2026.

programs.name: Lovable Ambassadors
programs.product: AI app builder for shipping web apps from natural language.
programs.whatTheyDo: Four published lead types: City (meetups and local campaigns), Campus (workshops and activations), Industry (adoption in a domain), Educator (teaching, office hours, livestreams). Host, teach, and pass community feedback to the team.
programs.eligibility: People already shipping on Lovable who host, teach, or organize. City leads are described as organizers with a track record of filling a room.
programs.perks: Free Pro account, meetup cost reimbursement and event toolkit, direct line to the team, amplification, private ambassador community.
programs.statusNote: Official hub: applications are now closed (closed 14 Aug 2026).

programs.name: Tangem Ambassador
programs.product: Crypto hardware wallet for self-custody. Not an AI product — filed under Other.
programs.whatTheyDo: Advocate for simple self-custody: share experience, create content, join campaigns and local initiatives, attend conferences, and help people understand how to manage assets.
programs.eligibility: People who already use and like Tangem. Typeform application; about 7+ minutes.
programs.perks: Not itemized on the public Typeform intro. Do not assume hardware or pay unless the form states it.
programs.statusNote: Typeform is accepting responses as of 31 Aug 2026.

programs.name: Appwrite Heroes
programs.product: Open-source backend platform (auth, databases, storage, functions, messaging) for apps.
programs.whatTheyDo: Build, write, speak, and help other developers ship with Appwrite; act as a leader in the Appwrite developer community.
programs.eligibility: Developers who already teach or help others on Appwrite. Confirm the current apply path — the historic /heroes URL now resolves to the main product site.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on official Appwrite community pages. /heroes did not render a live program form on the check of 30 Aug 2026.

programs.name: Auth0 Ambassador
programs.product: Identity and access management for applications (login, SSO, tokens).
programs.whatTheyDo: Share knowledge on identity and security through meetups, conferences, written content, webinars, and other events.
programs.eligibility: Historically a named ambassador program. The listed URL now lands on the Auth0 Developer Center rather than a live ambassador form.
programs.statusNote: Confirm whether a named ambassador program is still open. Do not treat the Developer Center as an apply form.

programs.name: AWS Community Builders
programs.product: Amazon’s public cloud: compute, storage, data, and AI services.
programs.whatTheyDo: Share AWS knowledge in writing and in person; join sessions with AWS product teams; grow online and local AWS communities. Limited members per year.
programs.eligibility: AWS technical enthusiasts and emerging thought leaders. All AWS builders may apply when the window is open.
programs.statusNote: Program is active (member directory is live). Apply windows are periodic — confirm on the Community Builders page.

programs.name: AWS Heroes
programs.product: Amazon’s public cloud.
programs.whatTheyDo: Recognition program for experts who already share AWS knowledge online and in person. Typically nomination/recognition rather than a cold apply form.
programs.eligibility: Established AWS community impact. Check the Heroes page for the current nomination path.
programs.statusNote: Recognition program. Confirm nomination process on the official Heroes page.

programs.name: AWS Student Builder Campus Leader
programs.product: AWS Builder Center, brought onto campus.
programs.whatTheyDo: Paid, part-time student ambassadors who host events, create content, and introduce peers to AWS cloud tools.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Official list notes the paid role is currently available in the United States, India, and Brazil.
programs.statusNote: Student-only and geo-limited. Confirm the current hiring window on Builder Center.

programs.name: AWS Student Builder Group Leader
programs.product: AWS Student Builder Groups (formerly AWS Cloud Clubs).
programs.whatTheyDo: Student leaders who found and run a campus AWS group: grow membership, host events, support local initiatives.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Formerly Cloud Club Captains.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm apply/launch steps on the Student Builder Groups page.

programs.name: BrowserStack Champions
programs.product: Cloud platform for testing websites and apps across real browsers and devices.
programs.whatTheyDo: QA and testing experts who share knowledge, keep learning in public, and raise the quality conversation in their communities.
programs.eligibility: Practitioners in software quality and testing. Confirm current apply/nomination on the Champions page.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on the official Champions page.

programs.name: Cloud Native Ambassadors (CNCF)
programs.product: Home of Kubernetes and the broader cloud-native open-source ecosystem.
programs.whatTheyDo: Advocate for cloud-native projects, mentor, and further CNCF’s open-source mission. Directory of current ambassadors is public.
programs.eligibility: People already leading in the cloud-native community. Follow the “Interested in becoming an Ambassador?” path on the CNCF page.
programs.statusNote: Program is active. Confirm the current application or nomination window on cncf.io.

programs.name: Cloudinary Ambassadors
programs.product: Media platform for images, video, and a visual web (upload, transform, deliver).
programs.whatTheyDo: Share digital-media expertise and advocate for better visual-web practice; typically content, talks, and community help.
programs.eligibility: High-level mastery of digital media technologies. Confirm apply path on the ambassadors page.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on cloudinary.com/ambassadors.

programs.name: Commudle Experts
programs.product: Platform for developer communities, events, and labs.
programs.whatTheyDo: Help other builders on Commudle; qualification and location are explicitly not the filter — published work is.
programs.eligibility: Students or professionals; freelancers, full-time, DevRel. Work samples matter more than title.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on the Experts program page.

programs.name: Cypress Ambassadors
programs.product: Frontend testing tool for web applications.
programs.whatTheyDo: Share Cypress knowledge through posts, webcasts, conferences, meetups, and other events.
programs.eligibility: People already teaching or speaking about Cypress. Confirm current apply window.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on cypress.io/ambassadors.

programs.name: DigitalOcean Navigators
programs.product: Cloud infrastructure aimed at developers and small teams (droplets, Kubernetes, managed DBs).
programs.whatTheyDo: Create content, code, and community events related to DigitalOcean products.
programs.eligibility: Builders already writing, coding, or organizing around DigitalOcean. Confirm the current Navigator apply window.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on the Navigators page.

programs.name: Docker Captains
programs.product: Container platform for building, sharing, and running applications.
programs.whatTheyDo: Technical experts and community builders who teach Docker, contribute, and help shape the product.
programs.eligibility: Established Docker educators and contributors. Typically invitation/nomination. Confirm on the Captains page.
programs.statusNote: Recognition program. Confirm nomination or apply path on docker.com.

programs.name: Figma User Group Leader
programs.product: Collaborative interface-design and product-design tool.
programs.whatTheyDo: Run a Friends of Figma / user group: host local or online gatherings so designers can connect and learn.
programs.eligibility: Organizers who can sustain a local Figma community. This is a user-group lead role, not a generic content-ambassador title.
programs.statusNote: Confirm leader applications on friends.figma.com.

programs.name: GitHub Campus Experts
programs.product: Git hosting, collaboration, and Education benefits for schools.
programs.whatTheyDo: Student leaders who build inclusive campus spaces to learn, share, and ship projects together.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Apply through GitHub Education docs.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm the current Expert application window in GitHub Education docs.

programs.name: GitHub Stars
programs.product: GitHub — code hosting and the public open-source network.
programs.whatTheyDo: Recognized community leaders who already inspire, educate, and shape developer communities. The public CTA is to nominate someone.
programs.eligibility: Impactful developers with a public teaching or community record. Nomination-led.
programs.statusNote: Nomination program. Confirm the current nomination form on stars.github.com.

programs.name: GitLab Heroes
programs.product: DevSecOps platform (git, CI/CD, security, and planning in one product).
programs.whatTheyDo: Recognize and support people who already make outstanding contributions to GitLab and its wider community.
programs.eligibility: Existing GitLab community contributors. Confirm the current Heroes join path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply or nomination status on about.gitlab.com/community/heroes/.

programs.name: GitKraken Ambassador
programs.product: Git GUI client and related Git productivity tools.
programs.whatTheyDo: Share knowledge about Git and the GitKraken client with other developers.
programs.eligibility: People who already teach Git / GitKraken. Confirm the live apply form.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on gitkraken.com/ambassador.

programs.name: Google Developer Experts
programs.product: Google’s developer platforms (Android, Cloud, Firebase, Web, AI, and more).
programs.whatTheyDo: Experienced practitioners recognized by Google who support other developers, startups, and companies. Invitation/nomination culture.
programs.eligibility: Established public technical leadership in a Google technology area. Follow the official Experts apply/nomination path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm the current Experts application or nomination window on developers.google.com/community/experts.

programs.name: Google Developer Groups Organizer
programs.product: Google developer technologies (Android, Cloud, Maps, and related APIs).
programs.whatTheyDo: Organize a local GDG chapter — meetups and talks around Google developer tools. Not a classic employee-style ambassador title. Campus variant (GDG On Campus) is student-only.
programs.eligibility: Chapter organizers. Student/university version is GDG On Campus.
programs.statusNote: Confirm chapter-organizer steps on the GDG page. On Campus is a separate student program.

programs.name: Google Women Techmakers Ambassador
programs.product: Google’s Women Techmakers community and resources for women in technology.
programs.whatTheyDo: Ambassadors who run WTM community activity and give other women in tech visibility, community, and resources.
programs.eligibility: Women-only ambassador track. Confirm current ambassador apply steps on the WTM site.
programs.statusNote: Women-only. Confirm apply status on developers.google.com/womentechmakers.

programs.name: HashiCorp Ambassadors
programs.product: Infrastructure tools including Terraform, Vault, Nomad, and Consul.
programs.whatTheyDo: Share knowledge of HashiCorp tools through content and local events, and give product feedback while following HashiCorp principles.
programs.eligibility: People already teaching HashiCorp tools in public. Confirm the current ambassador window.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on hashicorp.com/ambassadors.

programs.name: Intel Student Ambassador
programs.product: Intel developer tools, hardware, and software for students building with Intel technologies.
programs.whatTheyDo: Undergraduate and graduate students who promote learning, sharing, and collaboration in developer communities around Intel tech.
programs.eligibility: Students only.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm the current program window on Intel’s developer ambassadors page.

programs.name: Ionic Developer Expert
programs.product: Cross-platform app framework (Ionic, Capacitor) for web-to-mobile apps.
programs.whatTheyDo: Experts, influencers, and educators who already lead in the Ionic ecosystem and contribute to the wider developer community.
programs.eligibility: People with public Ionic expertise. Confirm current IDE program status.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on ionic.io/developer-experts.

programs.name: Kong Champions
programs.product: API gateway and API lifecycle platform (Kong Gateway, Konnect).
programs.whatTheyDo: Frequent contributors who blog, speak at local events, join user calls, and help on forums.
programs.eligibility: People already active in Kong’s community. Confirm Champion apply/nomination.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on konghq.com/community/kong-champions.

programs.name: MATLAB Student Ambassador
programs.product: MATLAB and Simulink — numerical computing and model-based design.
programs.whatTheyDo: Represent MathWorks on campus: host MATLAB/Simulink events and engage students on social. Published as a paid ~5 hrs/week role.
programs.eligibility: Students only.
programs.statusNote: Student-only paid campus role. Confirm the current hiring term on the MathWorks page.

programs.name: Microsoft MVP
programs.product: Microsoft developer and IT products (Azure, M365, GitHub, Power Platform, and more).
programs.whatTheyDo: Award for technical community leaders who already teach Microsoft technologies. Nomination-based recognition, renewed on a cycle.
programs.eligibility: Sustained public community contributions. Follow the official nomination process — not a casual open apply.
programs.statusNote: Nomination award. Confirm the current nomination cycle on mvp.microsoft.com.

programs.name: Microsoft Student Ambassador
programs.product: Microsoft Cloud and AI tools for students (Azure, GitHub, Copilot, and related student resources).
programs.whatTheyDo: Student leaders who build AI-driven projects with Microsoft technology and grow campus communities.
programs.eligibility: Students only.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm the current Student Ambassador apply window.

programs.name: MongoDB Community Advocacy
programs.product: Document database (Atlas and self-managed MongoDB).
programs.whatTheyDo: Champions and creators who advocate for MongoDB users through content, events, and community support.
programs.eligibility: Passionate MongoDB users. Program has champions and creators subdivisions. Confirm current join path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on mongodb.com/community/advocacy/.

programs.name: Notion Ambassadors
programs.product: All-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, projects, and databases.
programs.whatTheyDo: Volunteer enthusiasts who teach Notion: lead local communities, run events, produce courses and templates, and translate.
programs.eligibility: People already teaching Notion in public. Confirm the current ambassador apply path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on the Notion Ambassadors page.

programs.name: Notion Campus Leaders
programs.product: Notion workspace, taught on university campuses.
programs.whatTheyDo: Students who teach Notion and build a campus community around it.
programs.eligibility: Students / university campus leaders.
programs.statusNote: Student/campus program. Confirm the current Campus Leaders window.

programs.name: Nx Champions
programs.product: Monorepo and build platform (Nx) for JavaScript/TypeScript codebases.
programs.whatTheyDo: Publish content, share Nx expertise, and gather community feedback for the product team.
programs.eligibility: People already teaching Nx. Confirm Champion apply/nomination on the community page.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on nx.dev/community.

programs.name: NVIDIA University Ambassadors
programs.product: NVIDIA training in AI, accelerated computing, and data science (DLI workshops).
programs.whatTheyDo: Bring free instructor-led NVIDIA workshops to a university so students can take official DLI courses on campus.
programs.eligibility: University educators / campus program — not a general public meetup ambassador seat. Gated to the higher-ed context.
programs.statusNote: University/educator program. Confirm eligibility on NVIDIA’s University Ambassador page.

programs.name: OutSystems Ambassador
programs.product: Low-code platform for building enterprise applications.
programs.whatTheyDo: Recognized customer and community leaders who share how they build with OutSystems and join VIP expert access.
programs.eligibility: Established OutSystems practitioners. Confirm current ambassador path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on outsystems.com/ambassador-program/.

programs.name: Postman Supernovas
programs.product: API platform for designing, testing, and sharing APIs.
programs.whatTheyDo: Organize meetups, teach workshops, and help others learn APIs and Postman.
programs.eligibility: Leaders passionate about APIs, testing, and creating. Confirm the current Supernovas apply window.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on the Supernovas program page.

programs.name: Postman Student Programs
programs.product: Postman API platform, taught to students and educators (Student Expert, Student Leader, classroom programs).
programs.whatTheyDo: Student experts and leaders who spread API literacy on campus and in class.
programs.eligibility: Students and educators only.
programs.statusNote: Student/educator programs. Confirm current tracks on postman.com/student-program/.

programs.name: SAS Student Ambassador
programs.product: SAS analytics and statistical software.
programs.whatTheyDo: Selected students who use SAS in innovative work; travel stipend and visibility in the SAS community as published.
programs.eligibility: Students only, typically in data analytics and related fields.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm the current cohort window on the SAS academic page.

programs.name: Stack Overflow Student Ambassador
programs.product: Public Q&A network for programmers, plus Stack Overflow for Teams.
programs.whatTheyDo: Represent Stack Overflow on campus, bring classmates onto the platform, complete challenges, and help plan future semesters.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Listed as an early / first-cohort style program on the student site — confirm whether a new cohort is open.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm whether a cohort is open on students.stackoverflow.co.

programs.name: Streamlit Advocates
programs.product: Python framework for turning data scripts into shareable web apps.
programs.whatTheyDo: Create and share Streamlit content and videos, with training materials and one-on-one support from the program.
programs.eligibility: People who already make Streamlit content. Confirm the current Advocate apply path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on streamlit.io/community/advocates.

programs.name: Streamlit Creators
programs.product: Python data-app framework.
programs.whatTheyDo: Recognition for people who already help users, ship notable apps, or build Streamlit components — more honor roll than open apply.
programs.eligibility: Community members who have already set themselves apart. Confirm whether there is an open apply versus recognition-only.
programs.statusNote: Often recognition-based. Confirm on streamlit.io/creators.

programs.name: Tableau Ambassador
programs.product: Data visualization and business-intelligence platform.
programs.whatTheyDo: Active Tableau users recognized for forums, social teaching, and speaking.
programs.eligibility: Established Tableau community contributors. Confirm the current ambassador path.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply or nomination status on the Tableau community-leaders page.

programs.name: Twilio Champions
programs.product: Communications APIs (SMS, voice, email, WhatsApp) for developers.
programs.whatTheyDo: Developer ambassadors who teach Twilio in public and join focus groups / product feedback.
programs.eligibility: Developers already creating with or teaching Twilio. Confirm current Champions apply window.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on twilio.com/en-us/champions.

programs.name: Unleash Ambassadors
programs.product: Open-source feature-flag and experimentation platform.
programs.whatTheyDo: Share DevOps and feature-flag practice through meetups, conferences, writing, and webinars.
programs.eligibility: People teaching feature flags / Unleash in public. Confirm the live apply form.
programs.statusNote: Confirm apply status on getunleash.io/ambassador-program.

programs.name: X Student Ambassadors
programs.product: X social platform and X developer community.
programs.whatTheyDo: Student leaders who build campus community around X and receive mentorship and training. Check whether a chapter already exists locally.
programs.eligibility: Students only. Confirm whether the program is still operating — the developer URL is historical.
programs.statusNote: Student-only. Confirm on the X developer community whether the student ambassador program is still active.
